character-count.title: Character Count
character-count.seoDescription: Count characters in Japanese, English, and emoji instantly. Check counts without spaces or line breaks, lines, paragraphs, English words, and UTF-8 bytes. No sign-up required.

guide.title: How to use and count characters
guide.intro: Type or paste your text to see the character count immediately. This free tool works on phones and computers, with no account required.

counting.question: How are spaces, line breaks, and emoji counted?
counting.answer: Each visible character counts as one, whether it is full-width or half-width. Each of あ, A, 😊, and the combined family emoji 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 counts as one character. The main count includes spaces and line breaks. The second count excludes half-width and full-width spaces, tabs, and line breaks. If a submission has its own counting rules, check those requirements.

details.question: Can I also check word and byte counts?
details.answer: Open More counts to see lines, paragraphs, English words, and UTF-8 bytes. The English word count counts groups of Latin letters. Bytes measure data size: A uses 1 byte and あ uses 3 bytes in UTF-8.

draft.question: Is my text saved?
draft.answer: Counting runs in your browser without sending the text to a server for processing. Your text is not automatically saved and is cleared when you reload or leave the page. After Clear all, you can use Undo until you enter new text.

character-count.placeholder: Type or paste your text here
character-count.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the text and use your browser's Copy command.
character-count.pasteFailed: Could not paste. Use the text field's menu or your keyboard shortcut.
character-count.countingNote: “あ”, “A”, and “😊” each count as one character. Spaces and line breaks also count as one.

detailNotes.lines: Lines separated by line breaks, including blank lines.
detailNotes.paragraphs: Blocks of text separated by blank lines.
detailNotes.words: Latin-letter groups. Each of don't and well-known counts as one word.
detailNotes.utf8Bytes: Size of the full text, with LF line breaks (1 byte each).

qr-code.title: QR Code Generator
qr-code.seoTitle: QR Code Generator {'|'} Free PNG Download
qr-code.seoDescription: Create a QR code from a URL or text for free, with no sign-up. Copy the image or download a 1024px PNG. Generate your QR code instantly in your browser.

guide.title: How to create and save a QR code
guide.intro: Enter a URL or text to generate a QR code immediately. This free tool works on phones and computers, with no account required. Copy the resulting image or save it as a PNG.

image.question: Can I change the image size or error correction?
image.answer: To keep things simple, the image is fixed to a black-and-white 1024×1024-pixel PNG with the common error correction level M (approximately 15% data restoration). The pattern density adjusts automatically to your input, with a white margin at least four modules wide on every side. The on-screen preview is scaled down. Longer text creates a denser pattern, so display or print the saved PNG at a sufficient size and check that it scans before distributing it. If image copying is unavailable, use Save PNG.

draft.question: Is my input saved?
draft.answer: QR generation runs in your browser without sending your input to a server for processing. Your input is not added to this page's URL or automatically saved. Reloading or moving to another tool clears it. To share a QR code, copy the image or save it as a PNG. The image contains your input, so check its content before sharing. This site uses Google Analytics for traffic analysis and Google AdSense for advertising.

pi-lab.title: Pi Experiments
pi-lab.descriptionShort: Animations show the properties of pi and how to calculate it.
pi-lab.description: Animations show the properties of pi and how to calculate it.
pi-lab.seoTitle: Pi Experiments — Monte Carlo, Polygons, Rolling Circles, and Area
pi-lab.seoDescription: Estimate pi with random points and polygons, roll a circle to compare circumference with diameter, and rearrange sectors to see why circle area is πr².
pi-lab.reducedMotion: Autoplay is disabled while reduced motion is enabled. Manual controls remain available.

monte.title: Monte Carlo method
monte.description: Estimate pi from the share of random points inside the circle.
monte.visual: A circle inscribed in a square. Blue points are inside the circle; orange points are outside.
monte.limit: The exact counting limit has been reached. Reset to run another trial.
monte.drawingLimit: The diagram displays up to the first {count} points.
monte.graphAlt: The horizontal axis is total points N; the vertical axis is the estimate of pi. The scale narrows in steps as estimates converge, down to a range of 3.14 to 3.143. The dashed line marks pi; the solid line tracks the estimate.

polygon.title: Regular polygon approximation
polygon.description: Approximate the circle’s circumference with polygon perimeters, then divide by its diameter to estimate pi.
polygon.visual: A circle with inscribed and circumscribed regular polygons of {sides} sides. The inscribed polygon is solid blue; the circumscribed polygon is dashed orange. The circle’s diameter is {diameter}.
polygon.visualCircle: Inscribed and circumscribed regular {sides}-gons, drawn as circles because of their many sides. Values use the selected polygons’ perimeters. The circle’s diameter is {diameter}.
polygon.interval: The interval containing pi is shown on a scale from {min} to {max}.
polygon.explanation: A regular polygon’s perimeter is its side length times its number of sides. As you add sides, its perimeter approaches the circle’s circumference. Dividing by the circle’s diameter gives an approximation of pi. Inscribed polygons give smaller values and circumscribed polygons give larger ones, so you can also check the approximation’s accuracy. Archimedes used this approach. Displayed bounds are rounded outward to keep pi inside the interval.

wheel.title: Rolling circle
wheel.description: Roll the circle once without slipping. The distance traveled is its circumference; divide it by the diameter to get pi.
wheel.visual: A circle with diameter {diameter} rolls right without slipping. It has made {turns} turns. The horizontal dimension line crosses the center and joins both edges, showing the diameter. The blue spoke and rim marker show rotation. The blue arc matches the distance traveled. The upper scale shows distance; the lower scale shows distance divided by diameter.
wheel.complete: One full turn: circumference ÷ diameter ≈ π

area.title: Circle area
area.description: Cut the circle into sectors and rearrange them without changing its area. Finer cuts bring the shape closer to a rectangle.
area.visual: A circle divided into {count} equal sectors, arranged in alternating directions. Each curved boundary has half the circumference; each side is one radius long. In the rearranged view, a dashed rectangle has width πr and height r. More cuts bring the shape closer to that rectangle.
area.formulaAlt: Circle area equals pi times radius times radius, or pi times radius squared.

ants.title: Ant Observation
ants.descriptionShort: An observation box: add food and walls, and watch foraging trails emerge.
ants.description: Place food, draw walls, and watch ants form foraging trails.
ants.seoTitle: Ant Observation {'|'} Food and Pheromone Simulation
ants.seoDescription: Observe 300 ants finding food by following nearby pheromones. Choose brush sizes to add food, draw walls or erase them, and watch foraging paths change.
ants.hint: Choose a tool and brush size, then tap or drag in the box. Walls avoid the nest and food.
ants.canvasLabel: Ant observation box. Edit food and walls using the selected tool.
ants.canvasFallback: Observation requires a browser with Canvas 2D support.
ants.hidden: Time is paused while this tab is hidden
ants.about: Blue marks food pheromones; orange marks home pheromones. Searching ants follow blue and leave orange, while ants carrying food follow orange and leave blue. Searching ants also respond to nearby food odors. Pheromones fade over time.

notices.canvas: Canvas 2D is unavailable. Open this page in a supported browser.

algorithm.world: The world has 240×160 cells and 300 ants, updated every 1/30 of a model second. Ant positions and headings are continuous; food, walls and pheromone concentrations are stored per cell. Both pheromone fields start at zero.
algorithm.exchange: Each update first checks for pickup and delivery at the current position. A searching ant on a food cell takes one item, turns 180 degrees and starts carrying it. Inside the nest radius of 5 cells, it delivers the item, turns 180 degrees again and resumes searching.
algorithm.sensors: Searching ants read blue food pheromones; carrying ants read orange home pheromones. Three sensors look straight ahead and 0.7rad (about 40 degrees) to either side, at an individual distance of 3.5–6.5 cells. A wall between the ant and a sensor point makes its reading zero.
algorithm.turn: Ants turn smoothly according to the difference between the left and right readings. A strong forward reading favors continuing straight. In the formula below, L, F and R are the left, forward and right concentrations, and Δθ is the heading change in radians per update. This rule applies when the strongest reading exceeds 0.0001.
algorithm.food: Searching ants also sense food odors within a distance of less than 8 cells. Nearby cells with more food contribute more strongly. The combined direction adds a turn of up to 1.2rad per second. Food behind walls or food that has been depleted contributes nothing.
algorithm.move: After adding a random turn, ants move at 5.85–12.15 cells per second. If a wall or the world boundary blocks the movement, they stay in place and turn by a random angle between 90 and 270 degrees. Ants do not collide with each other.
algorithm.individuality: Individual differences use a fixed coefficient q between 0.7 and 1.3, assigned at creation. Sensor distance is 5×q, and the concentration exponent is k=0.9/q. A higher q means a longer sensing distance and a weaker bias toward the strongest trail. Each ant also has independently fluctuating movement speed.
algorithm.deposit: Searching ants deposit home pheromones; carrying ants deposit food pheromones in their current cell on every update. The amount follows the formula below. For a searching ant, d is the distance actually walked since last being in the nest. For a carrying ant, it is the distance walked since the last pickup. Deposits decrease as the ant travels farther from its source.
algorithm.diffusion: After all ants move, existing pheromones diffuse into accessible cells above, below, left and right, then undergo evaporation before new deposits are added. The diffusion coefficient is 0.6 and the evaporation rate is 0.12 per second: each update multiplies concentrations by exp(-0.12/30). Without new deposits, the total halves in about 5.8 seconds. Pheromones cannot pass through walls, and each cell is capped at a concentration of 100.
algorithm.randomness: The turning fluctuation w changes each update as w=0.9×previous w+0.1×uniform random[-1,1]. Another random value adds a turn of 0.09×(uniform random[-1,1]+2w). This is multiplied by 1.5 when the strongest pheromone reading exceeds 0.001 or food odor is detected, and by 2.4 otherwise. Random turns remain active on trails; there is no fixed percentage of dedicated scouts.
algorithm.routes: Ants do not directly know the direction of the nest or food. They use nearby information, and ants exploring another route leave pheromones that can change the trails. Short routes allow quicker round trips and stronger deposits near the source, while unused trails fade. Finding the shortest route is not guaranteed.
algorithm.editing: The food brush adds 100 items per covered cell. Walls avoid the nest and food; the eraser removes only walls and food on the ground. Choosing an initial map beside Reset starts that layout paused. Later resets restore the selected map, clearing edits, pheromones, carried food, delivery counts and elapsed time. Speed and tool settings are kept.
algorithm.time: Elapsed time is model time. Playback speed changes the number of updates, keeping the rules of each update the same. Time stops while paused or while the tab is hidden. A fixed random seed gives the same result for the same map and the same actions at the same update counts.
